[1515](https://docs.rs#1515)    /// The input contains a string. The lifetime of the string is ephemeral and
[1516](https://docs.rs#1516)    /// it may be destroyed after this method returns.
[1517](https://docs.rs#1517)    ///
[1518](https://docs.rs#1518)    /// This method allows the `Deserializer` to avoid a copy by retaining
[1519](https://docs.rs#1519)    /// ownership of any buffered data. `Deserialize` implementations that do
[1520](https://docs.rs#1520)    /// not benefit from taking ownership of `String` data should indicate that
[1521](https://docs.rs#1521)    /// to the deserializer by using `Deserializer::deserialize_str` rather than
[1522](https://docs.rs#1522)    /// `Deserializer::deserialize_string`.
[1523](https://docs.rs#1523)    ///
[1524](https://docs.rs#1524)    /// It is never correct to implement `visit_string` without implementing
[1525](https://docs.rs#1525)    /// `visit_str`. Implement neither, both, or just `visit_str`.
[1526](https://docs.rs#1526)    fn visit_str<E>(self, v: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self::Value, E>
[1527](https://docs.rs#1527)    where
[1528](https://docs.rs#1528)        E: [Error](https://docs.rs#304),
[1529](https://docs.rs#1529)    {
[1530](https://docs.rs#1530)        [Err](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)(Error::[invalid_type](https://docs.rs#304)(Unexpected::[Str](https://docs.rs#358)([v](https://docs.rs#1526)), &[self](https://docs.rs#1526)))
[1531](https://docs.rs#1531)    }
[1532](https://docs.rs#1532)
[1533](https://docs.rs#1533)    /// The input contains a string that lives at least as long as the
[1534](https://docs.rs#1534)    /// `Deserializer`.
[1535](https://docs.rs#1535)    ///
[1536](https://docs.rs#1536)    /// This enables zero-copy deserialization of strings in some formats. For
[1537](https://docs.rs#1537)    /// example JSON input containing the JSON string `"borrowed"` can be
[1538](https://docs.rs#1538)    /// deserialized with zero copying into a `&'a str` as long as the input
[1539](https://docs.rs#1539)    /// data outlives `'a`.
[1540](https://docs.rs#1540)    ///
[1541](https://docs.rs#1541)    /// The default implementation forwards to `visit_str`.
[1542](https://docs.rs#1542)    #[inline]

[1550](https://docs.rs#1550)    /// The input contains a string and ownership of the string is being given
[1551](https://docs.rs#1551)    /// to the `Visitor`.
[1552](https://docs.rs#1552)    ///
[1553](https://docs.rs#1553)    /// This method allows the `Visitor` to avoid a copy by taking ownership of
[1554](https://docs.rs#1554)    /// a string created by the `Deserializer`. `Deserialize` implementations
[1555](https://docs.rs#1555)    /// that benefit from taking ownership of `String` data should indicate that
[1556](https://docs.rs#1556)    /// to the deserializer by using `Deserializer::deserialize_string` rather
[1557](https://docs.rs#1557)    /// than `Deserializer::deserialize_str`, although not every deserializer
[1558](https://docs.rs#1558)    /// will honor such a request.
[1559](https://docs.rs#1559)    ///
[1560](https://docs.rs#1560)    /// It is never correct to implement `visit_string` without implementing
[1561](https://docs.rs#1561)    /// `visit_str`. Implement neither, both, or just `visit_str`.
[1562](https://docs.rs#1562)    ///
[1563](https://docs.rs#1563)    /// The default implementation forwards to `visit_str` and then drops the
[1564](https://docs.rs#1564)    /// `String`.
[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)    #[inline]
[1566](https://docs.rs#1566)    #[cfg(any(feature = "std", feature = "alloc"))]
[1567](https://docs.rs#1567)    #[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(any(feature = "std", feature = "alloc"))))]
[1568](https://docs.rs#1568)    fn visit_string<E>(self, v: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/alloc/string/struct.String.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self::Value, E>

[1570](https://docs.rs#1570)        E: [Error](https://docs.rs#304),
[1571](https://docs.rs#1571)    {
[1572](https://docs.rs#1572)        [self](https://docs.rs#1568).[visit_str](https://docs.rs#1526-1531)(&[v](https://docs.rs#1568))

[1724](https://docs.rs#1724)/// Provides a `Visitor` access to each element of a sequence in the input.
[1725](https://docs.rs#1725)///
[1726](https://docs.rs#1726)/// This is a trait that a `Deserializer` passes to a `Visitor` implementation,
[1727](https://docs.rs#1727)/// which deserializes each item in a sequence.
[1728](https://docs.rs#1728)///
[1729](https://docs.rs#1729)/// # Lifetime
[1730](https://docs.rs#1730)///
[1731](https://docs.rs#1731)/// The `'de` lifetime of this trait is the lifetime of data that may be
[1732](https://docs.rs#1732)/// borrowed by deserialized sequence elements. See the page [Understanding
[1733](https://docs.rs#1733)/// deserializer lifetimes] for a more detailed explanation of these lifetimes.
[1734](https://docs.rs#1734)///
[1735](https://docs.rs#1735)/// [Understanding deserializer lifetimes]: https://serde.rs/lifetimes.html
[1736](https://docs.rs#1736)///
[1737](https://docs.rs#1737)/// # Example implementation
[1738](https://docs.rs#1738)///
[1739](https://docs.rs#1739)/// The [example data format] presented on the website demonstrates an
[1740](https://docs.rs#1740)/// implementation of `SeqAccess` for a basic JSON data format.
[1741](https://docs.rs#1741)///
[1742](https://docs.rs#1742)/// [example data format]: https://serde.rs/data-format.html
[1743](https://docs.rs#1743)#[cfg_attr(
[1744](https://docs.rs#1744)    not(no_diagnostic_namespace),
[1745](https://docs.rs#1745)    diagnostic::on_unimplemented(
[1746](https://docs.rs#1746)        message = "the trait bound `{Self}: serde::de::SeqAccess<'de>` is not satisfied",
[1747](https://docs.rs#1747)    )
[1748](https://docs.rs#1748))]
[1749](https://docs.rs#1749)pub trait [SeqAccess](https://docs.rs/serde_core/de/trait.SeqAccess.html)<'de> {
[1750](https://docs.rs#1750)    /// The error type that can be returned if some error occurs during
[1751](https://docs.rs#1751)    /// deserialization.

[1753](https://docs.rs#1753)
[1754](https://docs.rs#1754)    /// This returns `Ok(Some(value))` for the next value in the sequence, or
[1755](https://docs.rs#1755)    /// `Ok(None)` if there are no more remaining items.
[1756](https://docs.rs#1756)    ///
[1757](https://docs.rs#1757)    /// `Deserialize` implementations should typically use
[1758](https://docs.rs#1758)    /// `SeqAccess::next_element` instead.
[1759](https://docs.rs#1759)    fn next_element_seed<T>(&mut self, seed: T) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/option/enum.Option.html)<T::Value>, Self::Error>
[1760](https://docs.rs#1760)    where
[1761](https://docs.rs#1761)        T: [DeserializeSeed](https://docs.rs#803-812)<'de>;
[1762](https://docs.rs#1762)
[1763](https://docs.rs#1763)    /// This returns `Ok(Some(value))` for the next value in the sequence, or
[1764](https://docs.rs#1764)    /// `Ok(None)` if there are no more remaining items.
[1765](https://docs.rs#1765)    ///
[1766](https://docs.rs#1766)    /// This method exists as a convenience for `Deserialize` implementations.
[1767](https://docs.rs#1767)    /// `SeqAccess` implementations should not override the default behavior.
[1768](https://docs.rs#1768)    #[inline]
[1769](https://docs.rs#1769)    fn next_element<T>(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/option/enum.Option.html)<T>, Self::Error>

[1779](https://docs.rs#1779)        [None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

[1813](https://docs.rs#1813)/// Provides a `Visitor` access to each entry of a map in the input.
[1814](https://docs.rs#1814)///
[1815](https://docs.rs#1815)/// This is a trait that a `Deserializer` passes to a `Visitor` implementation.
[1816](https://docs.rs#1816)///
[1817](https://docs.rs#1817)/// # Lifetime
[1818](https://docs.rs#1818)///
[1819](https://docs.rs#1819)/// The `'de` lifetime of this trait is the lifetime of data that may be
[1820](https://docs.rs#1820)/// borrowed by deserialized map entries. See the page [Understanding
[1821](https://docs.rs#1821)/// deserializer lifetimes] for a more detailed explanation of these lifetimes.
[1822](https://docs.rs#1822)///
[1823](https://docs.rs#1823)/// [Understanding deserializer lifetimes]: https://serde.rs/lifetimes.html
[1824](https://docs.rs#1824)///
[1825](https://docs.rs#1825)/// # Example implementation
[1826](https://docs.rs#1826)///
[1827](https://docs.rs#1827)/// The [example data format] presented on the website demonstrates an
[1828](https://docs.rs#1828)/// implementation of `MapAccess` for a basic JSON data format.
[1829](https://docs.rs#1829)///
[1830](https://docs.rs#1830)/// [example data format]: https://serde.rs/data-format.html
[1831](https://docs.rs#1831)#[cfg_attr(
[1832](https://docs.rs#1832)    not(no_diagnostic_namespace),
[1833](https://docs.rs#1833)    diagnostic::on_unimplemented(
[1834](https://docs.rs#1834)        message = "the trait bound `{Self}: serde::de::MapAccess<'de>` is not satisfied",
[1835](https://docs.rs#1835)    )
[1836](https://docs.rs#1836))]

[1838](https://docs.rs#1838)    /// The error type that can be returned if some error occurs during

[1842](https://docs.rs#1842)    /// This returns `Ok(Some(key))` for the next key in the map, or `Ok(None)`
[1843](https://docs.rs#1843)    /// if there are no more remaining entries.

[1845](https://docs.rs#1845)    /// `Deserialize` implementations should typically use

[1847](https://docs.rs#1847)    fn next_key_seed<K>(&mut self, seed: K) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/option/enum.Option.html)<K::Value>, Self::Error>

[1863](https://docs.rs#1863)
[1864](https://docs.rs#1864)    /// This returns `Ok(Some((key, value)))` for the next (key-value) pair in
[1865](https://docs.rs#1865)    /// the map, or `Ok(None)` if there are no more remaining items.
[1866](https://docs.rs#1866)    ///
[1867](https://docs.rs#1867)    /// `MapAccess` implementations should override the default behavior if a
[1868](https://docs.rs#1868)    /// more efficient implementation is possible.

[1872](https://docs.rs#1872)    #[inline]
[1873](https://docs.rs#1873)    fn next_entry_seed<K, V>(

[1882](https://docs.rs#1882)        match [tri!](https://docs.rs/lib.rs.html#111)(self.next_key_seed(kseed)) {
[1883](https://docs.rs#1883)            [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(key) => {
[1884](https://docs.rs#1884)                let value = [tri!](https://docs.rs/lib.rs.html#111)(self.next_value_seed(vseed));
[1885](https://docs.rs#1885)                [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)([Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(([key](https://docs.rs#1883), [value](https://docs.rs#1884))))
[1886](https://docs.rs#1886)            }
[1887](https://docs.rs#1887)            [None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) => [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)([None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)),
[1888](https://docs.rs#1888)        }
[1889](https://docs.rs#1889)    }

[2088](https://docs.rs#2088)pub trait [VariantAccess](https://docs.rs/serde_core/de/trait.VariantAccess.html)<'de>: [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) {
[2089](https://docs.rs#2089)    /// The error type that can be returned if some error occurs during
[2090](https://docs.rs#2090)    /// deserialization. Must match the error type of our `EnumAccess`.
[2091](https://docs.rs#2091)    type Error: [Error](https://docs.rs#304);
[2092](https://docs.rs#2092)
[2093](https://docs.rs#2093)    /// Called when deserializing a variant with no values.
[2094](https://docs.rs#2094)    ///

[2284](https://docs.rs#2284)/// Converts an existing value into a `Deserializer` from which other values can
[2285](https://docs.rs#2285)/// be deserialized.
[2286](https://docs.rs#2286)///
[2287](https://docs.rs#2287)/// # Lifetime
[2288](https://docs.rs#2288)///
[2289](https://docs.rs#2289)/// The `'de` lifetime of this trait is the lifetime of data that may be
[2290](https://docs.rs#2290)/// borrowed from the resulting `Deserializer`. See the page [Understanding
[2291](https://docs.rs#2291)/// deserializer lifetimes] for a more detailed explanation of these lifetimes.
[2292](https://docs.rs#2292)///
[2293](https://docs.rs#2293)/// [Understanding deserializer lifetimes]: https://serde.rs/lifetimes.html
[2294](https://docs.rs#2294)///
[2295](https://docs.rs#2295)/// # Example
[2296](https://docs.rs#2296)///
[2297](https://docs.rs#2297)/// ```edition2021
[2298](https://docs.rs#2298)/// use serde::de::{value, Deserialize, IntoDeserializer};
[2299](https://docs.rs#2299)/// use serde_derive::Deserialize;
[2300](https://docs.rs#2300)/// use std::str::FromStr;
[2301](https://docs.rs#2301)///
[2302](https://docs.rs#2302)/// #[derive(Deserialize)]
[2303](https://docs.rs#2303)/// enum Setting {
[2304](https://docs.rs#2304)///     On,
[2305](https://docs.rs#2305)///     Off,
[2306](https://docs.rs#2306)/// }
[2307](https://docs.rs#2307)///
[2308](https://docs.rs#2308)/// impl FromStr for Setting {
[2309](https://docs.rs#2309)///     type Err = value::Error;
[2310](https://docs.rs#2310)///
[2311](https://docs.rs#2311)///     fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
[2312](https://docs.rs#2312)///         Self::deserialize(s.into_deserializer())
[2313](https://docs.rs#2313)///     }
[2314](https://docs.rs#2314)/// }
[2315](https://docs.rs#2315)/// ```
[2316](https://docs.rs#2316)pub trait [IntoDeserializer](https://docs.rs/serde_core/de/trait.IntoDeserializer.html)<'de, E: [Error](https://docs.rs#304) = value::[Error](https://docs.rs/value.rs.html#52-54)> {
[2317](https://docs.rs#2317)    /// The type of the deserializer being converted into.
[2318](https://docs.rs#2318)    type Deserializer: [Deserializer](https://docs.rs#945-1266)<'de, Error = E>;
[2319](https://docs.rs#2319)
[2320](https://docs.rs#2320)    /// Convert this value into a deserializer.
[2321](https://docs.rs#2321)    fn into_deserializer(self) -> Self::Deserializer;

[2388](https://docs.rs#2388)            [tri!](https://docs.rs/lib.rs.html#111)(write!(formatter, "{}", self.0));
[2389](https://docs.rs#2389)        }
[2390](https://docs.rs#2390)        [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)(())
[2391](https://docs.rs#2391)    }
[2392](https://docs.rs#2392)}

[8](https://docs.rs#8)/// A type that can be used to index into a `serde_json::Value`.
[9](https://docs.rs#9)///
[10](https://docs.rs#10)/// The [`get`] and [`get_mut`] methods of `Value` accept any type that
[11](https://docs.rs#11)/// implements `Index`, as does the [square-bracket indexing operator]. This
[12](https://docs.rs#12)/// trait is implemented for strings which are used as the index into a JSON
[13](https://docs.rs#13)/// map, and for `usize` which is used as the index into a JSON array.
[14](https://docs.rs#14)///
[15](https://docs.rs#15)/// [`get`]: Value::get
[16](https://docs.rs#16)/// [`get_mut`]: Value::get_mut
[17](https://docs.rs#17)/// [square-bracket indexing operator]: Value#impl-Index%3CI%3E-for-Value
[18](https://docs.rs#18)///
[19](https://docs.rs#19)/// This trait is sealed and cannot be implemented for types outside of
[20](https://docs.rs#20)/// `serde_json`.
[21](https://docs.rs#21)///
[22](https://docs.rs#22)/// # Examples
[23](https://docs.rs#23)///
[24](https://docs.rs#24)/// ```
[25](https://docs.rs#25)/// # use serde_json::json;
[26](https://docs.rs#26)/// #
[27](https://docs.rs#27)/// let data = json!({ "inner": [1, 2, 3] });
[28](https://docs.rs#28)///
[29](https://docs.rs#29)/// // Data is a JSON map so it can be indexed with a string.
[30](https://docs.rs#30)/// let inner = &data["inner"];
[31](https://docs.rs#31)///
[32](https://docs.rs#32)/// // Inner is a JSON array so it can be indexed with an integer.
[33](https://docs.rs#33)/// let first = &inner[0];
[34](https://docs.rs#34)///
[35](https://docs.rs#35)/// assert_eq!(first, 1);
[36](https://docs.rs#36)/// ```

[158](https://docs.rs#158)
[159](https://docs.rs#159)// The usual semantics of Index is to panic on invalid indexing.
[160](https://docs.rs#160)//
[161](https://docs.rs#161)// That said, the usual semantics are for things like Vec and BTreeMap which
[162](https://docs.rs#162)// have different use cases than Value. If you are working with a Vec, you know
[163](https://docs.rs#163)// that you are working with a Vec and you can get the len of the Vec and make
[164](https://docs.rs#164)// sure your indices are within bounds. The Value use cases are more
[165](https://docs.rs#165)// loosey-goosey. You got some JSON from an endpoint and you want to pull values
[166](https://docs.rs#166)// out of it. Outside of this Index impl, you already have the option of using
[167](https://docs.rs#167)// value.as_array() and working with the Vec directly, or matching on
[168](https://docs.rs#168)// Value::Array and getting the Vec directly. The Index impl means you can skip
[169](https://docs.rs#169)// that and index directly into the thing using a concise syntax. You don't have
[170](https://docs.rs#170)// to check the type, you don't have to check the len, it is all about what you
[171](https://docs.rs#171)// expect the Value to look like.
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//
[173](https://docs.rs#173)// Basically the use cases that would be well served by panicking here are
[174](https://docs.rs#174)// better served by using one of the other approaches: get and get_mut,
[175](https://docs.rs#175)// as_array, or match. The value of this impl is that it adds a way of working
[176](https://docs.rs#176)// with Value that is not well served by the existing approaches: concise and
[177](https://docs.rs#177)// careless and sometimes that is exactly what you want.
[178](https://docs.rs#178)impl<I> [ops::Index](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/ops/index/trait.Index.html)<I> for [Value](https://docs.rs/mod.rs.html#116-176)
[179](https://docs.rs#179)where
[180](https://docs.rs#180)    I: [Index](https://docs.rs#37-52),
[181](https://docs.rs#181){
[182](https://docs.rs#182)    type Output = [Value](https://docs.rs/mod.rs.html#116-176);
[183](https://docs.rs#183)
[184](https://docs.rs#184)    /// Index into a `serde_json::Value` using the syntax `value[0]` or
[185](https://docs.rs#185)    /// `value["k"]`.
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    ///
[187](https://docs.rs#187)    /// Returns `Value::Null` if the type of `self` does not match the type of
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    /// the index, for example if the index is a string and `self` is an array
[189](https://docs.rs#189)    /// or a number. Also returns `Value::Null` if the given key does not exist
[190](https://docs.rs#190)    /// in the map or the given index is not within the bounds of the array.
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    ///
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    /// For retrieving deeply nested values, you should have a look at the
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    /// `Value::pointer` method.
[194](https://docs.rs#194)    ///
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    /// # Examples
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    ///
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    /// ```
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    /// # use serde_json::json;
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    /// #
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    /// let data = json!({
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    ///     "x": {
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    ///         "y": ["z", "zz"]
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    ///     }
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    /// });
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    ///
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    /// assert_eq!(data["x"]["y"], json!(["z", "zz"]));
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    /// assert_eq!(data["x"]["y"][0], json!("z"));
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    ///
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    /// assert_eq!(data["a"], json!(null)); // returns null for undefined values
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    /// assert_eq!(data["a"]["b"], json!(null)); // does not panic
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    /// ```

[218](https://docs.rs#218)impl<I> [ops::IndexMut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/core/ops/index/trait.IndexMut.html)<I> for [Value](https://docs.rs/mod.rs.html#116-176)

[222](https://docs.rs#222)    /// Write into a `serde_json::Value` using the syntax `value[0] = ...` or
[223](https://docs.rs#223)    /// `value["k"] = ...`.
[224](https://docs.rs#224)    ///
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    /// If the index is a number, the value must be an array of length bigger
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    /// than the index. Indexing into a value that is not an array or an array
[227](https://docs.rs#227)    /// that is too small will panic.
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    ///
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    /// If the index is a string, the value must be an object or null which is
[230](https://docs.rs#230)    /// treated like an empty object. If the key is not already present in the
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    /// object, it will be inserted with a value of null. Indexing into a value
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    /// that is neither an object nor null will panic.
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    ///
[234](https://docs.rs#234)    /// # Examples
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    ///
[236](https://docs.rs#236)    /// ```
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    /// # use serde_json::json;
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    /// #
[239](https://docs.rs#239)    /// let mut data = json!({ "x": 0 });
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    ///
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    /// // replace an existing key
[242](https://docs.rs#242)    /// data["x"] = json!(1);
[243](https://docs.rs#243)    ///
[244](https://docs.rs#244)    /// // insert a new key
[245](https://docs.rs#245)    /// data["y"] = json!([false, false, false]);
[246](https://docs.rs#246)    ///
[247](https://docs.rs#247)    /// // replace an array value
[248](https://docs.rs#248)    /// data["y"][0] = json!(true);
[249](https://docs.rs#249)    ///
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    /// // inserted a deeply nested key
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    /// data["a"]["b"]["c"]["d"] = json!(true);
[252](https://docs.rs#252)    ///
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    /// println!("{}", data);
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    /// ```
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    fn index_mut(&mut self, index: I) -> &mut [Value](https://docs.rs/mod.rs.html#116-176) {
[256](https://docs.rs#256)        [index](https://docs.rs#255).[index_or_insert](https://docs.rs#51)([self](https://docs.rs#255))
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    }
